demo.name: Spinning Beach Ball on Flat Water

scene.description: A hollow 60 g beach ball (radius 0.15 m, I = 2/3*m*r^2 = 9e-4 kg.m^2) spinning at 20 rad/s about a horizontal axis is dropped from 0.85 m onto flat sea water. It uses the engine's sampled water forces (Engine::Water), as Petri does. At rest the ball floats with about 1 cm draft, so only a small part of its volume is wet. Added mass, wave radiation damping and wetted-surface drag should stop the ball bouncing within about a second and remove most of its spin, whatever its collision elasticity, because water is not a collision contact. The scene lowers the sleep thresholds so the ball stays awake while it drifts on the water.
